briefdescription.para: Return true if given column is part of primary key.

detaileddescription.para: If field number is less than 63, corresponding bit in column mask is tested. Otherwise, check whether 64-th bit in mask is set or not. If it is set, then iterate through key parts of primary index and check field number. In case it isn't set, there are no key columns among the rest of fields.

briefdescription.para: Return the PRIMARY KEY index of a table.

detaileddescription.para: Note that during parsing routines this function is not equal to space_index(space, 0); call since primary key can be added after seconary keys:
CREATE TABLE t (a INT UNIQUE, b PRIMARY KEY);
In this particular case, after secondary index processing space still lacks PK, but index[0] != NULL since index array is filled in a straightforward way. Hence, function must return NULL.

briefdescription.para: Prepare a 0-terminated string in the wptr memory buffer that does not contain a sequence of more than one whatespace character.

detaileddescription.para:
Routine enforces ' ' (space) as whitespace delimiter. When character ' or " was met, the string is copied without any changes until the next ' or " sign. The wptr buffer is expected to have str_len + 1 bytes (this is the expected scenario where no extra whitespace characters in the source string).
wptr
The destination memory buffer of size str_len + 1.
str
The source string to be copied.
str_len
The source string str length.

briefdescription.para: Generate code to determine next free secondary index id in the space identified by space_id.

detaileddescription.para: Overall VDBE program logic is following:
1 Seek for space id in _index, goto l1 if seeks fails. 2 Fetch index id from _index record. 3 Goto l2 4 l1: Generate iid == 1.. 6 l2: Continue index creation.
Note that we generate iid == 1 in case of index search on purpose: it allows on_replace_dd_index() raise correct error - "can not add a secondary key before primary".

memberdef.name: sql_src_list_enlarge

briefdescription.para: Expand the space allocated for the given SrcList object by creating new_slots new slots beginning at start_idx.

detaileddescription.para: The start_idx is zero based. New slots are zeroed.
For example, suppose a SrcList initially contains two entries: A,B. To append 3 new entries onto the end, do this: sql_src_list_enlarge(db, src_list, 3, 2);

After the call above it would contain: A, B, nil, nil, nil. If the start_idx argument had been 1 instead of 2, then the result would have been: A, nil, nil, nil, B. To prepend the new slots, the start_idx value would be 0. The result then would be: nil, nil, nil, A, B.

parameterdescription.para: Number of new slots to add to src_list->a[].
Index in src_list->a[] of first new slot.
